correctness.rationale: Two white non-bridge vertices in the same clique cannot be separated by a first force on either. Under the resulting one-per-clique restriction, the only possible four-white configuration has both bridge endpoints white and no first force. With three whites, either the opposite clique forces its white bridge endpoint and then forces across the bridge, or a non-bridge blue helper clears the opposite clique's lone white non-bridge vertex before the bridge force. In each case the last internal white is forced within its clique. The other triple cases follow by exchanging the sides, and every allowed smaller white set is a subset of an allowed triple, so follows by blue-set monotonicity. Both cliques have the required helpers for p,q≥3. Counting triples gives (p−1)+(q−1)+2(p−1)(q−1); counting pairs excludes precisely internal same-side pairs. This gives every coefficient and the minimum size. An independently written closure check matched the criterion and counts on all 14,400 subsets in the 16 ordered pairs 3≤p,q≤6; replay: python /workspace/branches/d6109c61-1838-413a-b817-f87179e5cdb6/recheck_barbell.py. The uniform conclusion comes from the proof, not the census.
residual_risks: The finite check does not cover larger orders or variants of the forcing rule; the proof covers precisely the stated family.
